name: Agent-society and wargame simulation forecasting for geopolitics date ladders
one_line: Multi-agent crisis rollouts turned into a curve over a ladder's deadlines, shrunk toward a reference-class hazard and traded against the price on fee-free geopolitics ladders; unproven, and the price already beats the base rate the simulation shrinks to.
maturity: Experimental; hobby bridges without scored records, the one self-scored pilot lost 0/16 to the market (non-geopolitics stress tests); adjacent wargaming literature negative on bias
requires_ai: yes; LLM actors and umpire run rollouts; shrinkage, blend and sizing deterministic
edge: Hypothetical: whole-ladder curve and tripwire playbooks on fee-free, 1-2c-spread ladders
capital: $1k-$10k; depth-capped (~$150 within 5c per rung), long lock-up
build_time: 4-8 weeks solo on top of file 21's pipeline
opportunity_size: 248 live ladders, 652 open rungs, $15.7M liquidity; ~$40k near-touch depth per pass; war-driven
expected_results: no public data, theoretical only; guess -2% to +1%/month before LLM costs
competition: free commoditised tooling (MiroFish 75k stars); price set by specialists, bots, insiders
flag: grey; war/violence contracts, insider-scrutinised category, restricted jurisdictions
validate: Post-cutoff replay, six arms incl. base rate and market; kill if shrunk sim = base rate
top_risk: Price beats the base rate the sim shrinks to; unstable LLM bias
solo_fit_reason: Cheap to kill-test on resolved ladders, but every public validation is null or negative, the market already beats the reference class (Brier 0.153 vs 0.198 at listing, 0.018 vs 0.088 one day out), rollouts cost $2-42 per ladder against $0.36-1.46 for a plain forecaster, near-touch depth is ~$150 per rung and proving a 2-point edge needs ~690 independent questions (most of a year).
speed_class: speed-insensitive: rollouts take 30-60 min; only the listing-day window has room
results_1k: forward test only; -$170 to -$20/month after LLM spend (guess)
min_capital: $0 until the kill test passes; ~$5k after (fixed LLM spend)
changes_made: Written 2026-09-29 with live checks: Gamma geopolitics events (439 live, 2,039 live+closed paged), date-ladder census (248 ladders, 652 open rungs, spreads, fee flags, monotonicity), CLOB books on 36 mid-priced rungs, CLOB prices-history on a 160-rung / 152-event resolved sample at four horizons, GitHub API stats and README reads for MiroFish, OASIS, hermes bridge, mirofish-calibration, Prophet, PolFish and repo searches, arXiv API abstracts for nine wargaming / simulation papers, Polymarket fee and taker-rebate docs, WEEX Hormuz 200-agent write-up and its Gamma outcome.

Maturity set to Experimental (brief hypothesis Emerging rejected per critic notes); 'shrunk sim = base rate only' pre-registered as the kill condition; boundary with file 70 drawn (70 = procedural / reference-class hazard without actors, and it is this file's shrinkage target).

Own finding: the market beats a leave-future-out base rate at every horizon (Brier 0.153 vs 0.198 at listing + 1 day, 0.045 vs 0.096 at seven days; all event-clustered CIs exclude zero); crude hazard blends do not improve on the price.

Own finding: live ladders are already monotone (1 mid inversion in 189 adjacent 'by' pairs, none executable), so 'ladder coherence' is not an open edge; near-touch depth is ~$150 per rung within 5c against a Gamma liquidity median of $11.3k.
Own finding: AXRZCE/Prophet (MiroFish pipeline) self-reports 0/16 sim wins against the market; the public Hormuz 200-agent run (47.9% vs 31% price) resolved No.
Own finding: CLOB /prices-history returns nothing for closed markets with interval=max and rejects startTs/endTs windows over 15 days.
Updated the brief's US-Iran ceasefire ladder figure: $4.67M lifetime volume and $400k liquidity on 2026-09-29 (brief: $1.45M / $377k on 09-20).

Cite-check + skeptic pass 2026-09-29 (23 numbered sources re-fetched or re-queried: 9 arXiv abstracts via the API, 7 GitHub repos + 6 repo searches + 5 more bridge READMEs, WEEX, mirofish.us, Gamma event 256854, fee and rebate docs, fresh Gamma geopolitics snapshot, CLOB prices-history behaviour; 4 pack refs and files 15/21/24/30 figures re-checked; 23 confirmed, 7 corrected, 0 removed, 0 unreachable): (1) own baseline re-run and re-conditioned on 'market open at the horizon' (observable) instead of 'open two days later' (future information), which had dropped 51 fast-resolving No rungs: one-day market Brier 0.018 (n=113) not 0.032, share base rate 0.101 / 0.088 at 7 / 1 days, headline BSS range -0.29 to -3.96; the time-aware constant-hazard arm ties the price at 7 and 1 days (CI includes zero; 7 and 3 Yes outcomes), so 'beats the reference class at every horizon' now applies to the share base rate only; (2) AXRZCE/Prophet's 0/16 were short-deadline hard-data, culture and price markets its author calls stress tests, not geopolitics; (3) power figure qualified: ~690 questions holds for a forecaster that departs from the price as much as the base rate does; (4) Shibboleth effect is -0.86 to +0.80 by model (not ±0.8); Solopova's cooperative finding is explanation framing, not drift in play; Lamparth's 'farcical harmony' and trait insensitivity added (scope item); (5) $143M anomalous profit is platform-wide, not 'mostly geopolitics' (E4); Maduro is one of two CFTC event-contract insider complaints, not 'the first'; France is ISP-blocked, not close-only; E9's war-bill item is Wikipedia-sourced; (6) running-cost arithmetic fixed (LLM $20-840/month, rows and monthly cost updated); one open ladder rung in ten under the geopolitics tag carries politics_fees. 15-field part 2,529 -> 2,414 words.
open_doubts: The evaluation sample is 160 rungs from 152 events; late horizons hold only 7, 7 and 3 Yes outcomes at 30 / 7 / 1 days, so late-horizon Brier gaps rest on a handful of events; the constant-hazard model is pooled across very different question types.
Prices from /prices-history are hourly points (last value at or before each horizon), not executable bid/ask; the proper-betting PnL in the validation plan needs a book recorder.
The 'rungs priced 15-35c resolve Yes 16.7% vs 23.7% priced' longshot pattern pools rung-horizons (84) that are not independent; it is indicative only.
Model refusals on military role-play are asserted by the brief and not measured here.
Rollout token counts (130k in / 16k out) are a design estimate, not a measurement; bridge-repo cost figures are self-reported.
A viral MiroFish-on-Polymarket profit claim surfaced in search snippets could not be traced to a wallet or primary post; it is treated as unverified and not used.
Liquidity-reward parameters appear on most open ladder rungs in Gamma, but pool sizes were not checked.
